findings.claim: The supplied router implements six foundation procedures: identity.session, identity.scopes, identity.entry and identity.syncCredentials are queries; identity.createInitialBond and authority.refreshSnapshot are commands. The capability catalog marks all six admitted for the app channel with session assurance and required G2 evidence.

All shown handlers require both identity and platform context. Security operations receive the caller's signal or a five-second timeout. syncCredentials reports SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE if its issuer is absent. These source-level mechanisms do not establish deployed execution or complete authorization coverage.

The literal empty-v1-contract description reflects the earlier reset checkpoint and is no longer an accurate description of the supplied router. Its narrower empty-business-contract statement remains consistent with the shown foundation-only procedures. The governing policy's two-read-only-identity-procedures description is also superseded by the six shown procedures, including two commands.

Foundation admission does not authorize implementing business procedures. Governing policy explicitly resumes horizontal engineering while deferring business admission, feature migrations and unresolved product-policy choices. Current implementation evidence changes the foundation inventory, not that scope decision.

G2 is a declared evidence requirement, not supplied proof of passing G2. The capability comment explicitly leaves owner confirmation of this bar pending. The historical catalog reports partial verification and separately lists hosted identity, deployment, R1, provider handlers, retention, reconciliation, feature admission and offline paths as outstanding; their present completion cannot be established here.
